correctness.rationale: For each fixed length-k marked path in a uniform Cayley tree, the rooted-forest count gives (k+1)n^(n-k-2) extensions. Deleting a marked endpoint leaf gives k(n-1)^(n-k-2) extensions, and deleting a specified nonpath leaf then choosing one of n-1 attachment vertices gives (k+1)(n-1)^(n-k-2). Summing exact conditional leaf probabilities proves F_n(k) for all 1<=k<=n-1; Prüfer coding independently yields the unconditional mean. Direct subtraction factors as 2r^(n-k-3)(n-N_k)/(n(k+1)(k+2)), with strictly increasing N_k; this proves the exact unique/double peaks and n^(1/3) scale. Uniform Taylor expansions from the exact F_n(k)/mean identity give the stated peak correction and k/sqrt(n) limit. Every boundary 1,n-1 and n>=4 is handled. A standalone verifier independently enumerates all labeled trees up to n=8 and passes 44755 checks; finite checks are supplementary, not the general proof.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Endpoint-degree regression does not by definition equal conditional total-leaf regression. Its one-endpoint leaf probability decreases with k, but the unobserved off-path vertices supply a nonconstant additional contribution. The total regression changes from increasing to decreasing near n^(1/3), whereas the endpoint-degree regression is monotone decreasing. Thus the cited endpoint-only statement does not itself state or logically imply the total regression without further enumeration of a separate observable.

originality.rationale: Classical labeled-forest extension counts are not presented as new. A full directly relevant published endpoint-degree conditioned-on-distance result was inspected and yields only one endpoint leaf probability; it does not provide off-path leaf contributions, total-leaf regression, cubic-root peak, precise double-peak orders, or the square-root baseline sign limit. The primary full texts examined address root-forest enumeration, Wiener indices, and leaf-marked distance profiles, without stating or directly covering this joint conditional expectation. Search nonmatches alone are not a proof of novelty; implicit consequences of general multivariate forest enumerators remain a historical-priority risk.
residual_risks: Classical multivariate enumerations for Cayley trees may contain implicit differentiation identities yielding the same conditional expected leaf count.

value.rationale: The global number of leaves measures the abundance of terminal vertices and tree branching, while the separation of two specified vertices measures global geometry. Unlike the local endpoint-leaf regression, total leaf expectation peaks at an intermediate distance with an exact cubic-root law, infinitely many discrete two-point ties, and a distinct square-root-scale baseline sign reversal. The result is a full finite-sample classification of two standard Cayley-tree observables rather than an arbitrary small enumerated instance, and it helps distinguish local and global effects in distance-conditioned tree statistics.
